title: Setting an anchor for someone else
header_line: My analysis of one book on neuro-linguistic programming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What do you want them to feel when they leave?
I said: now I will complicate it a little more. I ask you to evoke an anchor for somebody. Come up with one.
A student asked what the main emotions or aspects are that you want a person to feel, and what the result is.

I said that you cannot transfer an anchor from the taste to the description unless you make the transfer; then you cannot communicate it to other people. I then described a plate of fish so vividly the listeners could taste it.
I said that language of the senses, such as a delicate crust, a soft steaming flake, the balance of ocean and warmth and subtle seasoning, is what carries the anchor.

I described a call where I asked a question that the other person could not answer immediately, and the other tried to buy time, so I answered it myself with both. I said the pattern interruption triggered a little anxiety.
I said that knowing about the person from research gives you more options to set an anchor. I gave transparency and responsibility to clients as what I want to anchor.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the feeling you want to anchor for someone.
Write the sensory words for it.
Write what you know about them before you meet.
Write the pattern interruption you could use honestly.
Write the credibility words you will use.

check.q: What did I say you need to do with an anchor you want to share?
What kind of language carries the anchor?
What did I say knowing about the person gives you?
choices: More options to set an anchor

recap: Choose the feeling. Use sensory words. Use interruption honestly.
